title: Linear Search
statement: Find the index of a target element in an array.
inputOutputContract: Input n target on first line followed by n array elements. Return the first 0-based matching index or -1.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the returns one based index behavior in linearSearch; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of linearSearch: Search from index zero and return the first matching 0-based position; return -1 if absent.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `if (arr[i] == target) return i + 1;`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in returns one based index, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Search from index zero and return the first matching 0-based position; return -1 if absent.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `if (arr[i] == target) return i + 1;` with `if (arr[i] == target) return i;` in linearSearch, then retest T1–T6.
